RQ1.1: How do model architecture and training environment impact training energy consumption and GPU usage?

Santiago del Rey

Load and preprocess data

We load the data from the parquet file, filter out the inception_v3 architecture and the Desktop Normal User training environment, and normalize the energy consumption by the total number of images seen during training (converting MJ to J). We also prepare the gpu_usage variable.

df <- read_parquet("data/metrics/processed/clean-dl-training-energy-consumption-dataset.gzip") %>%
  filter(architecture != "inception_v3" & `training environment` != "Desktop Normal User") %>%
  mutate(
    energy = (`energy (MJ)` * 1000000) / `total seen images`, # Convert MJ to J and normalize by total seen images
    training_environment = factor(`training environment`, levels = c("Desktop ML Engineer", "Server")),
    architecture = case_match(
      architecture,
      "mobilenet_v2" ~ "Mobilenet V2",
      "nasnet_mobile" ~ "NASNet Mobile",
      "resnet50" ~ "ResNet50",
      "xception" ~ "Xception",
      "vgg16" ~ "VGG16"
    ),
    architecture = factor(architecture, levels = c("Mobilenet V2", "NASNet Mobile", "ResNet50", "Xception", "VGG16")),
    gpu_usage = `gpu usage (%)`
  ) %>%
  select(energy, gpu_usage, architecture, training_environment)
# Define a function to filter outliers of a given variable on an input data frame
filter_outliers <- function(df, variable) {
  df %>%
    group_by(architecture, training_environment) %>%
    mutate(
      Q1 = quantile(!!sym(variable), 0.25),
      Q3 = quantile(!!sym(variable), 0.75),
      IQR = Q3 - Q1,
      is_outlier = !!sym(variable) < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR) | !!sym(variable) > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(!is_outlier) %>%
    select(-Q1, -Q3, -IQR, -is_outlier)
}

filtered_energy_data <- filter_outliers(df, "energy")
# Outlier filtering for gpu_usage (by group)
filtered_gpu_data <- filter_outliers(df, "gpu_usage")

# Set sum-to-zero contrasts in each model call so that Type III tests do not depend on global options
sum_contrasts <- list(architecture = "contr.sum", training_environment = "contr.sum")

Energy Consumption Analysis

Data summary

filtered_energy_data %>%
  group_by(architecture, training_environment) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_energy = mean(energy, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_energy = sd(energy, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_energy = min(energy, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_energy = max(energy, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n()
  )
## `summarise()` has grouped output by 'architecture'. You can override using the
## `.groups` argument.

Visualize the data

Histograms of energy consumption

par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) # Set up a 1x2 grid for histograms
hist(filtered_energy_data$energy, main = "Raw Energy Consumption (J/image)", breaks = 30)
hist(log(filtered_energy_data$energy), main = "Log Energy Consumption (J/image)", breaks = 30)

Bar plot of energy consumption by architecture and training environment

median_energy_by_arch_env <- filtered_energy_data %>%
  group_by(architecture, training_environment) %>%
  summarise(median_energy = median(energy, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()
## `summarise()` has grouped output by 'architecture'. You can override using the
## `.groups` argument.
greenest_architecture <- median_energy_by_arch_env %>%
  filter(median_energy == min(median_energy)) %>%
  pull(architecture) %>%
  unique()
greenest_bar_height <- median_energy_by_arch_env %>%
  filter(architecture == greenest_architecture) %>%
  summarise(min_energy = min(median_energy)) %>%
  pull(min_energy)

max_median_energy <- max(median_energy_by_arch_env$median_energy)

dodge_width <- 0.9
env_levels <- levels(factor(filtered_energy_data$training_environment)) # preserves order
target_env <- "Desktop ML Engineer"

env_index <- which(env_levels == target_env)
n_envs <- length(env_levels)
offset <- dodge_width * ((env_index - 0.5) / n_envs - 0.5)

x_base <- as.numeric(factor(greenest_architecture))
x_pos <- x_base + offset

relative_improvement <- (max_median_energy - greenest_bar_height) / max_median_energy * 100
label_text <- paste0("↓ ", formatC(relative_improvement, format = "f", digits = 2), "%")

make_energy_plot <- function(annotation_font_size = 16) {
  annottation_size <- annotation_font_size / ggplot2::.pt # Convert to relative size
  ggplot(filtered_energy_data, aes(x = architecture, y = energy, fill = training_environment)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "summary", fun = "median", position = position_dodge()) +
    # Error bars show the interquartile range
    geom_errorbar(
      stat = "summary",
      fun.data = median_hilow,
      fun.args = list(conf.int = 0.5),
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
      width = 0.2
    ) +
    # Add a horizontal line for the maximum median energy consumption
    geom_hline(
      yintercept = max_median_energy,
      linetype = "dashed", color = "red"
    ) +
    # Add arrow pointing down
    geom_segment(
      aes(
        x = x_pos,
        xend = x_pos,
        y = max_median_energy,
        yend = greenest_bar_height + 0.005,
      ),
      arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm"), type = "closed"),
      color = "darkgreen",
      linewidth = 1,
      alpha = 0.7,
      inherit.aes = FALSE
    ) +
    # Add text label
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = x_pos + 0.3, # horizontal offset to the right of the arrow
      y = greenest_bar_height + (max_median_energy - greenest_bar_height) / 2, # vertical midpoint
      label = label_text,
      color = "darkgreen",
      fontface = "bold",
      size = annottation_size
    ) +
    labs(
      x = "Architecture",
      y = "Median Energy\nConsumption (J/image)",
      fill = "Training Environment"
    )
}

Linear Model

Fit a linear model to the energy consumption data, including an interaction term between architecture and training environment.

model_energy <- lm(energy ~ architecture * training_environment, data = filtered_energy_data, contrasts = sum_contrasts)
summary(model_energy)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = energy ~ architecture * training_environment, data = filtered_energy_data, 
##     contrasts = sum_contrasts)
## 
## Residuals:
##        Min         1Q     Median         3Q        Max 
## -0.0240405 -0.0030677  0.0002766  0.0031561  0.0297347 
## 
## Coefficients:
##                                       Estimate Std. Error  t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)                          0.2618972  0.0004137  633.103  < 2e-16 ***
## architecture1                       -0.1529125  0.0008023 -190.582  < 2e-16 ***
## architecture2                       -0.0037762  0.0008835   -4.274 2.66e-05 ***
## architecture3                       -0.0194231  0.0008074  -24.056  < 2e-16 ***
## architecture4                        0.0373426  0.0008185   45.621  < 2e-16 ***
## training_environment1               -0.0325269  0.0004137  -78.630  < 2e-16 ***
## architecture1:training_environment1  0.0022722  0.0008023    2.832 0.004972 ** 
## architecture2:training_environment1 -0.0435820  0.0008835  -49.329  < 2e-16 ***
## architecture3:training_environment1  0.0002498  0.0008074    0.309 0.757241    
## architecture4:training_environment1 -0.0028543  0.0008185   -3.487 0.000569 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.006875 on 272 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.9959, Adjusted R-squared:  0.9957 
## F-statistic:  7277 on 9 and 272 DF,  p-value: < 2.2e-16

Model diagnostics

sim_res_energy <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = model_energy)
testResiduals(sim_res_energy)

## alternative hypothesis: two.sided

##

##  expectations
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## outliers at both margin(s) = 10, observations = 282, p-value =
## 0.0001084
## alternative hypothesis: true probability of success is not equal to 0.007968127
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.01713353 0.06424551
## sample estimates:
## frequency of outliers (expected: 0.00796812749003984 ) 
##                                             0.03546099
check_model(model_energy)

The residual variance differs across cells, so we complement the classical tests with heteroscedasticity-consistent (HC3) tests.

leveneTest(energy ~ architecture * training_environment, data = filtered_energy_data)

Significance testing

Type III tests with sum-to-zero contrasts (set in the model call, so the warning effectsize gives for Type III tables does not apply). Effect sizes are computed from the Type III sums of squares.

anova_energy <- Anova(model_energy, type = 3)
anova_energy
Anova(model_energy, type = 3, white.adjust = "hc3") # robust to unequal variances
## Coefficient covariances computed by hccm()
effectsize::eta_squared(anova_energy, partial = FALSE, verbose = FALSE) # eta-squared
effectsize::eta_squared(anova_energy, partial = TRUE, verbose = FALSE) # partial eta-squared

Post hoc tests

emm_energy <- emmeans(model_energy, ~ architecture * training_environment, type = "response")
pair_comparison <- pairs(emm_energy, type = "response")

# To view results:
summary(emm_energy)
summary(pair_comparison)

Below we show the non-significant pairwise comparisons

pair_comparison_df <- as.data.frame(pair_comparison)
pair_comparison_df %>%
  filter(p.value > 0.05) %>%
  select(contrast, estimate, SE, df, t.ratio, p.value)

    data = emm_df,
    aes(x = architecture, ymin = lower_CI, ymax = upper_CI, color = training_environment, group = training_environment),
    width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = NULL,
    x = NULL,
    y = "Estimated Energy Consumption (J/image)",
    color = "Training Environment"
  ) +
  theme_pubr() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 14))

Sensitivity analysis: residual-based trimming

Earlier versions of this analysis removed the observations whose DHARMa scaled residuals fell outside the 2.5%–97.5% quantiles. This rule always removes about 5% of the data, so we only report it as a sensitivity check.

trim_by_scaled_residuals <- function(model, data) {
  scaled_res <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = model)$scaledResiduals
  outlier_index <- which(scaled_res < quantile(scaled_res, 0.025) | scaled_res > quantile(scaled_res, 0.975))
  list(removed = data[outlier_index, ], kept = if (length(outlier_index) > 0) data[-outlier_index, ] else data)
}

trimmed_energy <- trim_by_scaled_residuals(model_energy, filtered_energy_data)
trimmed_energy$removed %>% count(architecture, training_environment)
model_energy_trimmed <- lm(energy ~ architecture * training_environment, data = trimmed_energy$kept, contrasts = sum_contrasts)
anova_energy_trimmed <- Anova(model_energy_trimmed, type = 3)
anova_energy_trimmed
effectsize::eta_squared(anova_energy_trimmed, partial = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
